question.text: Mohandas Gandhi was an advisor and mentor to this first prime minister of an independent India.
question.clue: This man said his countrymen would "awake to life and freedom" in an address he gave on the night of his country's independence called the "Tryst with Destiny" speech.

swap.leadin: Babur founded this empire after a victory at the First Battle of Panipat.
swap.text: Name this Muslim empire centered at Agra that was expanded and strengthened by Akbar the Great in the sixteenth century.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this dynasty killed his half-brother Dara Shikoh and gave his head to his father, whom he imprisoned in the Agra Fort.

question.leadin: This country became the first Muslim-majority democracy to be led by a woman when Benazir Bhutto led the PPP to victory in 1988 elections.
question.text: Name this country where Bhutto was assassinated in 2007 at a campaign rally in Rawalpindi.
question.clue: At a 2007 rally, a female leader of this country and daughter of former leader Zulfikar Ali was assassinated at a political rally in Rawalpindi.

swap.leadin: It was built by the Jamuna River by Shah Jahan for his third wife.
swap.text: Name this white marble mausoleum with a prominent dome in Agra, India.
swap.clue: The most famous view of this building is of its south side and shows its main dome along with a pair of smaller domes on each side as well as the four white minarets on each corner of its square base.

question.leadin: Name the following about the Chola [t'SHO-rah] Empire.
question.text: The Chola dynasty was of this ethnic group. This ethnic group's namesake tigers committed terrorist attacks in modern-day Sri Lanka.
question.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

swap.text: Timur also raided this city, whose namesake sultanate was later led by Ibrahim Lodi. This city contains the modern-day capital of India.
swap.clue: Flaming camels were employed in an attack on this city by Tamerlane, and this city's Red Fort was built after it was made the capital of the Mughal Dynasty by Shah Jahan.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about an empire from Indian history FTPE.
question.text: This emperor was the grandson of Babur. His advisors included Birbal and Bairam Khan. He won the second battle of Panipat and pursued diplomacy with the Rajput caste.
question.clue: This ruler married a Rajput woman named Manmati and abolished the jizya.

swap.leadin: Identify the following Mughal rulers from descriptions.
swap.text: This emperor won a power struggle with his brother Dara Shikoh and had his father Shah Jahan imprisoned. The execution of Sambhaji, the son of the Maratha chief Shivaji, would prove to be his undoing.
swap.clue: This ruler was denounced in an "epistle of victory," or Zafarnama, written by Gobind Singh.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Britain's relations with India, per part.
question.text: John Holwell claimed that 126 Europeans died when placed here after the nawab Siraj-ud-Dawlah forced the surrender of Holwell's garrison.
question.clue: This event's 123 victims primarily died of heat exhaustion in Fort William, where they had been captured by the Nawab of Bengal.

swap.text: When Portugual refused to give up Goa, Nehru sent Krishna Menon to take it, which he did in just two days in this 1961 operation. This word, which derives from the Sanskrit for "victory," also identifies India's operations in the Kargil War.
swap.clue: The Indian high command referred to the annexation of Goa under the codename "Operation [this word]". An operation named for this word also refers to Indian military actions in the Kargil War.

question.leadin: Along with Daman and Diu ("dee-yoo"), this region was annexed in an invasion by K. P. Candeth.
question.text: Name this former Portuguese colony that was annexed in 1961 as part of Operation Vijay. Afonso de Albuquerque conquered this region for the Portuguese Empire in 1510.
question.clue: Colony state, which was seized in Operation Vijay, is where Francis Xavier proselytized and is buried.

swap.leadin: Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw said that "If a man says he is not afraid of dying, he is either lying or he is [one of these people]."
swap.text: Name this group of people who have served in dedicated units in the British Army since 1857. Kulbir Thapa was the first of these largely-Nepali soldiers to be awarded a Victoria Cross.
swap.clue: These soldiers, who wield the khukuri machete, share a name with a historic kingdom on the Indian subcontinent located along the Trishuli River.

question.text: The Venus of Hohle Fels was found in one of these places. Paintings of bulls are frequently found on the walls of these places, which include Lascaux ("lass-KO") and Altamira.
question.clue: That one of these locations is named for the thousand Buddha statues that it contains.

swap.text: William Digby estimated that 100,000 people starved in Mysore and this city, during a famine sometimes named for it, whilst Victoria feasted. The British East India Company divided India into three Presidencies named for Bengal, Bombay, and this city.
swap.clue: This city's namesake army faced the Vellore Mutiny.

question.text: Similar theories about the occupation of Northern India often propose that survivors of the Indus Valley Civilization fled South to establish three kingdoms in the Deccan: Chera, Pandya, and this largest Tamil empire.
question.clue: This kingdom in Southern India that at its height extended its rule to the Malay peninsula. This kingdom was defeated by the Pandyas in the 13th century.

swap.leadin: This empire's crown prince was slain on elephantback in the Battle of Takkolam by Butuga II of the Western Gangas during a war against the Rashtrakuta Empire.
swap.text: Name this empire whose Emperor Rajendra I finally conquered the Rashtrakutas. While crown prince of this empire for his father, Rajaraja the Great, Rajendra also annexed the Sri Lankan kingdom of Anuradhapura.
swap.clue: The Maldives and the competing Pandya dynasty were conquered by Rajaraja I of this empire, who later built the Brihadisvara ] Temple.

question.text: Aw Barkhadle may have also spread Islam to this present-day country. Arabic partially inspired the right-to-left Thaana ("TAH-nuh") script for this country's Dhivehi ("dih-VAY-hee") language.
question.answerHtml: Maldives [or Republic of Maldives; accept Maldive Islands or Sultanate of Maldives]
question.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

swap.text: The famine also hit this historical region, where earlier events included the Battle of Seringapatam and British campaigns against Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan.
swap.clue: This kingdom's last sultan successfully used rockets with attached blades in the Battle of Pollilur but died in 1799 while defending Seringapatam.

question.leadin: In 1997, a president from this family ordered a mammoth offensive codenamed Operation Certain Victory, which failed.
question.text: Name this family of Chandrika Kumaratunga, or CBK. Her father Solomon, known as the "Silver Bell of Asia," was assassinated by a Buddhist monk in 1959, after which, her mother Sirimavo became the world's first female prime minister as chair of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party.
question.answerHtml: Bandaranaike [or Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga, Solomon West Ridgeway Dias Bandaranaike, or Sirima Ratwatte Dias Bandaranaike]
question.clue: This surname of Solomon, who was assassinated by a Buddhist monk after he signed a pact with the leader of the Federal Party. The first woman to become a prime minister in Asia had this last name.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a group of people comprised of 36 clans. FTPE.
swap.text: Claiming to be descendents of the original Kshatriya, these Hindu peoples held Northern India during the Middle Ages. Their dynasties included the Chauhan and Sisodias, and they were incorporated into the Mughal Empire as part of a marriage-based alliance with Akbar.
swap.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.
